description: Check tax amounts against a rate schedule the caller supplies. When a declared amount disagrees, the other inclusivity formula is tried too: if that one gives the declared figure, the finding says the policy and the data disagree rather than that the arithmetic is wrong, which is a different correction. Also reports a code absent from the schedule, a line rate disagreeing with it, and an amount too precise for the currency. Not tax advice. Pay 180000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

base.description: The amount tax is computed on. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

tax_amount.description: The declared tax, compared against the computed one. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

tax_rate.description: A rate on the line, which takes precedence and whose disagreement with the schedule is reported. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

minor_units.description: Decimal places per currency code, overriding the published table. Two is the default because most currencies have two.

rounding.description: How a figure is rounded. Required rather than defaulted in spirit: half-up and half-even disagree on every price ending in 5, so the mode is an accounting policy and is published in the response. Defaults to half_up when omitted.

tax_inclusive.description: Whether the base already includes tax. Defaults to false.

schedule.description: The rates in force, as the caller states them. This product applies them and never supplies them.

rate.description: As a percentage. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

name: tax_computation_audit

arithmetic_sound.description: True only when every rate resolved, every declared amount matched and every figure fitted the currency.

by_tax_code.description: Per code: lines, base and tax, which is the shape a return is prepared from.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.
